failures.criterion: (1) A browser update's append takes 6 Postgres round trips, not 10
failures.evidence: 7 at a7a4239d. Counted with the tester's TCP proxy, $TMPDIR/tester556/rtproxy (it counts a round trip each time the client speaks after the server, and names each statement's SQL from Parse/Bind; GET /reset and /stats on its control port), between the server and the pod's Postgres. A real envoy-dispatch process (throwaway multiprocess test, startPair through the proxy), warm keystroke: pg_advisory_lock | begin | pg_advisory_xact_lock | gate read | one batch (insert into doc_updates, doc_settlements_pending, doc_pending_authors) | commit | pg_advisory_unlock. The docs package's Service gave the same 7 for 20 of 20 keystrokes. The old append at 97e5e32d, counted the same way, is 10. The surplus is round trip 3: since main's #2496 a browser keystroke is stored through PgVersioned.AppendRoomFlush (persistence.go:192), which holds the room's session advisory lock (withRoomLock), and Service.flushThrough (flush.go:199) calls AppendRoomUpdateTx (persistence.go:258) with roomLocked=false, so appendUpdateTxClass takes pg_advisory_xact_lock again (persistence.go:327-330). 99117932's skip of that lock applies to appendUpdate, which the browser path no longer reaches after the merge. AppendRoomUpdateTx is also reached from Ledger.flushThrough inside live writes, which hold no session lock, so the flush must say whether its caller holds the lock. No red test is written: no hook in the store lets a test count statements, and the user-visible bound (1 s) holds. The proxy run above reproduces it. Evidence: https://github.com/sjawhar/legion/pull/2414 (round-18 tester comment)
